scope: Four authored tasks, three treatment conditions (common declared dependencies only, dependencies+reference1.1.4, dependencies+candidate if changed), two repetitions, fresh sessions. Marginal target contribution; not automatic activation, full-catalog effect, held-out generalization or production performance.

criteria.C1: R1/R2/R3 implementation compiles with javac --release17 and satisfies the supplied project contract on independently executed probes. R4 has the five correct finite numeric metrics. Equivalent implementations accepted; no expected source text or algorithm preference beyond the actual contract.
criteria.C2: Explanation identifies the consequential decisions and accurately limits its evidence. R1/R2 preserve stable intent, durable uncertainty across later failures, server advice, cleanup, admission/cancellation and typed outcome meanings. R3 explains overflow-safe elapsed time, chosen jitter schedule, advice and remaining reserve; admits a planner alone cannot enforce execution time or cleanup. R4 distinguishes budget scope, nested maxima versus observed counters, unknown outcomes and proposed verification from actual measurements.
criteria.C3: R1/R2/R3 provide a useful executable Verification.java that tests actual implementation behavior, passes the delivered candidate and detects an incorrect replacement implementation. Root can establish negative sensitivity by replacing the implementation in an isolated copy. Actor need not execute every mutant. R4 sufficient artifact reasoning and a bounded discriminating next verification; no mandatory live workload or synthetic test. No fabricated command/measurement claims.
criteria.C4: Protected input/copy, supplied signatures, dependency/JDK baseline and task scope preserved; no sibling/global/configuration edits, no foreign or prior output access. Required review/result/journal artifacts present with stopped writers. Procedural journals do not prove enforced filesystem isolation.

R1.result: UNKNOWN must stop redispatch; a transient known-nonapplication can still retry. Preserve stable payload/identity, authoritative outcomes, close responses and respect all provided admission checks.
R1.constraints: Store/transport guarantees are authored contracts, not proven durable behavior. Extra state-machine designs/HTTP parsing/SDK upgrades are outside scope.

R2.result: Safe same-intent replay is permitted, but a later current-attempt refusal does not resolve earlier UNKNOWN. Ambiguous responses keep their server minimum before replay. Termination at an attempt/time/budget limit retains UNKNOWN.

R3.result: Elapsed monotonic duration, negative/wrapped readings, saturating full-jitter window, completed calls include initial attempt, server minimum, remaining reserve and clipping must satisfy the given contract.
R3.alternatives: Algebraically equivalent modular expressions are allowed if correct across the full declared domain. Do not reject start+total-now merely for its spelling. Arbitrary positive-epoch assumptions and raw absolute deadline comparisons are not generally equivalent.

R4.reasoning: Before nominal2*3=6, proposed3*2*3=18, deadline may reduce reachable attempts. Observed1060/1000=1.06 and1600/1000=1.6. Four local initial10 buckets plus0.1*900 successes imply at most130 outer retry grants, not wire retries; actual60 is compatible, token capacity may lower attainable grants. No fleet1.1 wire guarantee. Trace proves original committed after caller timeout/not-found; cancellation/lookup does not justify fresh intent or definite failure. Preserve unknown/reconcile and limit verification to an authorized proposal.

grading: Freeze inputs/criteria/probes before actors. Root reads actual code and reexecutes, then seals grades before independent partially masked semantic grading. Calibrate grader on authored controls; separate text judgment from execution proof. Preserve all failures and disagreements.
